notes: Historical team and organization events, 1950-2026, for the fully historical scenario and as conditional proposals in other modes. Each summary is a paraphrase of a page that was opened for this file. When date_precision is year, only the year is attested and the month and day are 01 placeholders. When date_precision is month, the day is 01. constructorId is the Jolpica id when that id exists in the engine table. A null constructorId has constructor_id_null_reason. Organizations that lineage.json keeps apart (the two Alfa Romeo works teams and the later Sauber rename, the two Hondas, the two Mercedes, the Viry Renault team and Enstone, the two Aston Martins, the two ATS teams, Team Lotus and Lotus Racing and Lotus F1) are separate organization values even when they share a constructorId. Differences from lineage.json are listed in the gaps and in the pull request, not silently 'corrected' there.
gaps: PP-046 is not in VISION.md yet (open issue 48). These rows are the historical proposals described in DESIGN section 2.4 and PP-004.
Engine-specific Jolpica ids (cooper-climax, lotus-ford, brabham-repco, mclaren-ford, eagle-climax, and the same pattern) are not separate organizations and have no founding or folding rows.

Lola's championship season blocks are listed on the constructors page, but the company page does not make them one team. No entry or exit row pretends they are. The company founding and 2012 closure are rows with a null constructor id.

Politoys and Iso-Marlboro are names of Frank Williams Racing Cars, taken from that page, not separate organizations. The engine table still has politoys and iso_marlboro ids, and the rows use those ids.
The 1976 Wolf-Williams season is filed in the engine table under both williams and wolf. The rename row uses wolf. It does not create a second team.
No Turner constructor page existed at the title that was requested. Hall is named on the Indy-only list with no article and no seasons. Both stay out of the event rows.

Indy builders whose pages do not give championship seasons: Dunn (a tenth place in 1955 is stated, not the season list), Epperly, Kuzma, Moore, Nichels, Rae, Snowberger, Stevens, Del Roy. Ewing is recorded only for the 1960 pole car.
The Oracle title on Red Bull and the Mastercard title on McLaren are current names on those pages, without a start year in the sections read.
Mild Seven's last Benetton season is not isolated. The page shows the name continuing on later engine rows.
Fiat's purchase of Ferrari is not in the Ferrari page lead that was read, so it is not a row.
Routine customer engine changes for every other team are already in engines.json and are not copied here.
Privateer entrants who never built a chassis (Rob Walker, and the rest of that list) are not constructors and are not rows, except where one of them later became a constructor (Tyrrell, Williams).

events.summary: Aguri Suzuki founded Super Aguri, based in Tokyo and run from the old Arrows factory at Leafield. It raced from the 2006 Bahrain Grand Prix as an unofficial Honda second team.
events.preconditions: Honda had a senior team and a former driver who could front a second entry using an existing British factory.

events.summary: Toro Rosso debuted in 2006 as Red Bull's junior team, based in Faenza. Before the season Dietrich Mateschitz agreed a 50/50 share with Gerhard Berger, and Red Bull bought Berger's share back in late November 2008.
events.preconditions: The Minardi purchase provided the entry. The second team existed to prepare drivers for Red Bull Racing.

events.summary: After BMW bought Sauber and the partnership ended, Williams used Cosworth V8s in 2006.
events.preconditions: The works partner had left to run its own team. Cosworth was an available customer engine.

events.summary: Red Bull used Renault engines from 2007 through 2018. From 2016 to 2018 the same engines were badged TAG Heuer after the relationship soured in 2015.
events.preconditions: Renault was a works supplier that would sell to a second team. The later badge was a broken relationship, not a new maker.

events.summary: Spyker F1 raced the 2007 season under a Dutch licence. At the end of the year it was sold to Vijay Mallya and renamed Force India.
events.preconditions: Spyker Cars had owned the team for one season. The page presents the sale as the end of that ownership, not as a new licence application.

events.summary: In 2007 McLaren signed a seven-year Vodafone contract and raced as Vodafone McLaren Mercedes. At the 2013 Australian Grand Prix the team said the deal would end that year.
events.preconditions: A telecoms company could replace a banned tobacco sponsor. The end was announced before the contract's original last year.

events.summary: Williams announced a switch from Cosworth to Toyota for 2007, including Toyota's electronics and battery package.
events.preconditions: 2006 had been a poor Cosworth season. Toyota was a manufacturer with engines and no title, willing to supply a second team.

events.summary: In October 2007 a consortium led by Vijay Mallya and Michiel Mol bought Spyker F1 for 88 million euros. The team raced as Force India from 2008 under an Indian licence.
events.preconditions: The buyers were paying for an existing Silverstone entry. Force India's own constructor record starts the following season.

events.summary: Force India raced from the 2008 Australian Grand Prix. The infobox's last race under that constructor is the 2018 Hungarian Grand Prix.
events.preconditions: The October 2007 purchase gave the new owners a winter to rename the entry.

events.summary: The team withdrew after four races in 2008 because of money. The last race is the 2008 Spanish Grand Prix. It scored four points, all in 2007.
events.preconditions: A second team without its own manufacturer budget could not survive once the funding stopped.

events.summary: Honda announced in December 2008 that it was leaving, citing the financial crisis, and looked for a buyer while the 2009 car was already in design.
events.preconditions: The team still had a factory and a nearly finished car, but the manufacturer no longer wanted to fund it. Toyota and BMW Sauber are described as staying through 2009 before they too left.

events.summary: BMW left after 2009 and sold the team back to Peter Sauber. The page cites an uncompetitive 2009 car, the financial crisis, and rules that did not help road-car technology.
events.preconditions: The works team was missing the results that justified a factory budget, and the founder was willing to take it back.

events.summary: Ross Brawn's management buyout of the Honda team, described as a symbolic 1 pound sale from Hiroshi Oshima, created Brawn GP for 2009. Honda left about 100 million dollars and Mercedes supplied engines as a customer.
events.preconditions: Honda was leaving and the 2009 car was already designed. A buyer who could take the factory and fit a Mercedes engine could keep the entry alive for one season.

events.summary: After 2009 Peter Sauber bought the team back from BMW for one euro, and it raced again under the Sauber name.
events.preconditions: BMW wanted out and the founder would take the company back for a token price, debts and all.

events.summary: Before the 2009 Brazilian Grand Prix, Williams said the three-year Toyota deal would end. Toyota then left Formula One entirely.
events.preconditions: The customer deal had not made Williams a front-runner, and the supplier was about to quit the sport.

events.summary: On 4 November 2009 Toyota announced an immediate withdrawal after eight seasons without a Grand Prix win. The infobox's last race is the 2009 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.
events.preconditions: The page contrasts the size of the budget with the missing win. It does not describe a buyer for the entry.

events.summary: On 16 November 2009 Mercedes-Benz and Aabar Investments bought 75.1 percent of Brawn GP. The team was renamed Mercedes for 2010.
events.preconditions: Mercedes was already the engine supplier, Honda had left a funded car, and Brawn had just won both 2009 titles, so the buyer was taking over a proven entry rather than starting one.

events.summary: Adrian Campos founded the Spanish team. Jose Ramon Carabante bought it before the 2010 debut, and Thesan Capital bought it in July 2011.
events.preconditions: A new 2010 entry changed hands before it raced. Each buyer was taking a fragile new team, not a works manufacturer.

events.summary: Tony Fernandes' group, using a licence from Proton to use the Lotus name, raced as Lotus Racing in 2010. The entry came after BMW withdrew in 2009. In 2011 the team bought the historic Team Lotus name.
events.preconditions: A 2010 slot existed because a manufacturer team had left. The Lotus name was a licence, not Colin Chapman's team.

events.summary: The former Brawn team raced as Mercedes from 2010. This is not the 1954-1955 Stuttgart works team.
events.preconditions: Mercedes and Aabar already owned the majority after November 2009, and Mercedes was the engine supplier.

events.summary: From 2010 the team was an independent constructor again and bought customer Ferrari engines. It raced as Sauber until the Alfa Romeo rename.
events.preconditions: The one-euro buyback kept the Hinwil entry alive without a manufacturer owner.

events.summary: Manor Grand Prix was renamed Virgin Racing at the end of 2009 after Virgin bought a share and the naming rights. It raced in 2010 under a British licence and in 2011 under a Russian licence.
events.preconditions: One of the 2010 entries was available to a new group. Virgin's money bought the name on a Manor-run team, not a works manufacturer.

events.summary: For 2010 Williams took an updated Cosworth V8 after the Toyota contract ended.
events.preconditions: A supplier had left and Cosworth was again the available customer engine.

events.summary: At the end of 2010 Marussia Motors bought a stake and became the main sponsor. The 2011 name was Marussia Virgin Racing.
events.preconditions: A Russian sportscar firm could buy into a backmarker that had no points and no title sponsor strong enough to refuse.

events.summary: By 2011 Renault had sold its shares in the Enstone team, which still used the Renault chassis name that year, and stayed in the sport as an engine supplier.
events.preconditions: Renault could keep the engine business without owning the team. The page says the chassis name did not change in the same year as the share sale.

events.summary: In October 2011 Sahara India Pariwar bought 42.5 percent of Force India for 100 million dollars. The team later raced as Sahara Force India.
events.preconditions: A minority shareholder with that much cash could put its name on a midfield team that already had a grid slot.

events.summary: Fernandes had bought Caterham Cars. The Formula One team was renamed Caterham for 2012 and raced under a Malaysian licence through 2014.
events.preconditions: The group owned both the entry and the sportscar brand. The rename followed the end of its right to use the Lotus name.

events.summary: The owners could not sell the team by 30 November 2012 and it was left off the 2013 entry list. The last race is the 2012 Brazilian Grand Prix.
events.preconditions: No buyer by the FIA's deadline meant no entry. The page does not describe a merger.

events.summary: Lola Cars stopped operations in 2012. That is the company, decades after the last Formula One season block on the constructors list.
events.preconditions: The firm had been a racing-car maker, not an active Grand Prix team, when it closed.
events.constructor_id_null_reason: No Lola Formula One constructor id in 2012.

events.summary: The Enstone team raced as Lotus F1 from 2012 to 2015, named for branding partner Group Lotus and majority-owned by Genii Capital. It is not Team Lotus and not Caterham.
events.preconditions: Renault had sold the shares and the team still had an entry. A licensed Lotus brand gave it a name for four seasons.

events.summary: The team was renamed Marussia for 2012 and raced with a Russian licence through 2014.
events.preconditions: Marussia was already the main sponsor and a shareholder. The Virgin name was no longer needed on the entry.

events.summary: On 4 July 2011 Williams said Renault would supply engines from 2012.
events.preconditions: Cosworth was not the engine Williams wanted for the new rules era. Renault was an active manufacturer.

events.summary: Vodafone's title deal ended after 2013. From 2015 to 2017 the team raced as McLaren Honda because of the engine partnership, and from 2018 as McLaren Formula 1 Team after the team principal said he would not sell the name to a title sponsor.
events.preconditions: The sponsor chose to leave. Honda's name on the team was the engine contract, not a new title-sponsor sale. The current 'McLaren Mastercard' name has no start date in the sections read.

events.summary: In May 2013 Williams signed a long-term Mercedes deal for the 2014 1.6-litre V6 turbos.
events.preconditions: The hybrid rules needed a manufacturer power unit. Mercedes had one and Williams did not.

events.summary: In July 2014 Fernandes and his partners said they had sold the team to a Swiss and Middle Eastern consortium. The Caterham name was then used under licence.
events.preconditions: The original owners were leaving. A new consortium still needed the brand licence to keep the name.

events.summary: In October 2014 Caterham entered administration and missed the United States Grand Prix, then the Brazilian Grand Prix. It crowd-funded a return for the Abu Dhabi finale.
events.preconditions: The new owners did not have the cash to travel to every remaining race. Administration is what took the cars off the road.

events.summary: On 7 October 2014 Marussia filed notice in the London High Court that it intended to enter administration. It missed the United States Grand Prix, and on 7 November 2014 the administrator said the team had ceased trading, owing about 60 million pounds.
events.preconditions: The team had one points finish and then a fatal crash for Jules Bianchi, and it did not have the money for the remaining races.

events.summary: Honda has built hybrid power units again since 2015. The engine list's current Honda block starts that year.
events.preconditions: The return is an engine programme. McLaren raced as McLaren Honda in 2015-2017 because of that supply, not because Honda owned the team.
events.constructor_id_null_reason: Power-unit supply; Honda did not field its own constructor id.

events.summary: McLaren raced as McLaren Honda from 2015 to 2017 because Honda supplied the power unit.
events.preconditions: A works engine partner was willing to put its name on the team. It was not a change of ownership.

events.summary: The team left administration on 19 February 2015 after a rescue and raced 2015 as Manor Marussia, still using the Marussia constructor name and a British licence. Stephen Fitzpatrick is described as the purchaser.
events.preconditions: The entry was still on the provisional list and the cars existed. New money could restart a team that had ceased trading, which is a rescue rather than a new application.

events.summary: On 27 February 2015 the FIA's revised entry list dropped Caterham and put Manor Marussia back. By March the Caterham assets were up for auction.
events.preconditions: A team in administration that missed races could not show it would start the next season. The entry was removed rather than sold on as a going concern.

events.summary: Gene Haas established Haas Formula LLC in April 2014. The team debuted in 2016 and is still racing, now presented as TGR Haas F1 Team.
events.preconditions: A NASCAR owner funding a new American-licensed team, with a Banbury forward base and a design office in Maranello. Ferrari supplies the power unit.

events.summary: Haas has used Ferrari power units since its debut. The team keeps a design office in Maranello.
events.preconditions: A new team could buy a works manufacturer's supply and technical proximity instead of building an engine.

events.summary: In January 2016 the team was renamed Manor Racing and used the constructor name MRT. John Booth and Graeme Lowdon had left the Formula One project at the end of 2015.
events.preconditions: The rescued team could drop the Marussia constructor name once it had its own 2016 entry. The original Manor Motorsport company was no longer running it.

events.summary: In 2016 Peter Sauber sold his controlling stake to Finn Rausing, who changed the leadership and cancelled a switch to Honda engines.
events.preconditions: The private team was short of money even with Ferrari engines. A new majority owner could decide the engine contract.

events.summary: Renault bought the Enstone team again. Lotus F1 was sold back to Renault on 18 December 2015, and the Lotus name was dropped on 3 February 2016.
events.preconditions: Renault was still an engine manufacturer and Enstone was available. The December sale is the dated contract; the February announcement is the name change.

events.summary: Manor closed in March 2017, before the season, after a sale to a new owner did not happen.
events.preconditions: A small team that could not find a buyer had no budget for the first race. The page does not describe a merger.

events.summary: In 2018 Sauber signed Alfa Romeo as title sponsor. Alfa Romeo had no technical role. The full rename to Alfa Romeo Racing started in 2019.
events.preconditions: A historic badge was available as a sponsor for a Ferrari-powered private team. The deal did not make Alfa a manufacturer again.

events.summary: By July 2018, before the Hungarian Grand Prix, the London High Court put Force India into administration. The page says Vijay Mallya, accused of fraud and defaulting on loans, could not keep funding the team.
events.preconditions: The entry depended on an owner who had run out of money. Administration is what made a distress sale possible.

events.summary: In August 2018 a Lawrence Stroll-led group called Racing Point UK bought the Force India assets and entered the rest of 2018 as Racing Point Force India, still using the Force India constructor name.
events.preconditions: The old company was in administration, so the buyers purchased assets and a late entry rather than the original company. The grid slot for the rest of the year still needed the Force India name.

events.summary: The team raced as Alfa Romeo from 2019 through 2023. The Alfa Romeo page says the company ended the sponsorship after 2023 so the team could be taken over by Audi.
events.preconditions: The title deal was deep enough to change the constructor name, but the page is explicit that Alfa did not engineer the car. This is not the 1950 or 1979 Alfa works teams.

events.summary: Red Bull began using Honda engines in 2019.
events.preconditions: The Renault relationship had broken down. Honda had a hybrid programme and needed a front-running chassis after McLaren.

events.summary: In February 2019 the entry was renamed Racing Point. It debuted at the 2019 Australian Grand Prix and raced 2019 and 2020, including as BWT Racing Point.
events.preconditions: The asset purchase was done and a new constructor name could start at the next season. The page treats this as a new entry, not as a continuation of the 2008 Force India company.

events.summary: The team was renamed AlphaTauri for 2020 to advertise Red Bull's fashion brand. Tost and Marko described it as a sister team rather than only a junior team.
events.preconditions: Red Bull owned both teams. A rename did not need a new licence or a new factory.

events.summary: In August 2020 Dorilton Capital bought Williams, and Frank and Claire Williams left the management. The page says the company had been put up for sale in May 2020 after a 13 million pound loss.
events.preconditions: The founding family no longer had the results or the cash to keep the team. A buyer could take the Grove entry without inventing a new licence.

events.summary: The Enstone team was rebranded Alpine for 2021 to promote Renault's sports-car brand, and it kept the works-team role until Renault stopped as an engine manufacturer at the end of 2025.
events.preconditions: Groupe Renault already owned the team. The rename needed the Alpine brand, not a new entry or a new factory.

events.summary: Racing Point was rebranded Aston Martin for 2021. Lawrence Stroll's AMR GP Limited owns the team and Stroll is also an Aston Martin Lagonda shareholder. This is not the 1959-1960 David Brown works team.
events.preconditions: The group already owned the Silverstone entry and had a stake in the road-car company, so the rename advertised that brand.

events.summary: Honda's official works involvement ended after 2021, though complete engines kept arriving from Japan for Red Bull through 2025, partly under a Red Bull Powertrains badge.
events.preconditions: Red Bull had a championship-winning car and a contract for the hardware, so the engines could continue after Honda left as a named manufacturer.
events.constructor_id_null_reason: The ongoing supply was badged for Red Bull, not a Honda constructor entry.

events.summary: Audi said in 2022 that it intended to buy Sauber and use the Hinwil factory, ahead of the 2026 chassis and power-unit rules. The project added an engine site in Bavaria and a technology centre in England.
events.preconditions: A private Swiss team with a factory was available, and a known rule change gave a manufacturer a date to aim at.
events.constructor_id_null_reason: The constructor id remained sauber until the 2026 Audi entry.

events.summary: On 25 January 2022 Ineos took a one-third stake beside Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff, after an announcement in December 2020.
events.preconditions: The team was a going works entry. The deal is a share sale, not a rename or a new constructor.

events.summary: Alfa Romeo ended the sponsorship after 2023. The constructor id returned to Sauber for 2024 and 2025, when the team raced as Stake F1 Team Kick Sauber or Kick Sauber depending on local gambling-advertising law.
events.preconditions: The Alfa deal had an end date, and Audi's takeover was already agreed. A gambling sponsor could fill the name for the two seasons before 2026.

events.summary: Audi bought the team in 2024 to use it as the chassis and sporting base of a works entry. Sauber's own company is shown as ended on 7 December 2025.
events.preconditions: Sauber had already been racing under sponsor names and did not have a works power unit of its own. Audi needed an existing entry more than a new licence.

events.summary: In 2024 and 2025 the team used the Kick Sauber and Stake names. The Sauber company infobox ends on 7 December 2025.
events.preconditions: Audi owned the team but the works Audi name waited for the 2026 rules. A title sponsor covered the gap.

events.summary: The team was rebranded RB for 2024. The page says the commercial name became Racing Bulls in 2025, while the constructor identity used here stays rb.
events.preconditions: Red Bull still owned the Faenza team. The 2024 change is a name, not a sale.

events.summary: In October 2024 the Toyota name returned through a technical partnership with Haas, via Toyota Gazoo Racing. In December 2025 that became a title partnership and Haas was presented as TGR Haas F1 Team.
events.preconditions: Haas already had an American entry and a Ferrari power unit. Toyota did not take over the constructor.
events.constructor_id_null_reason: Partnership with Haas; the constructor id stays haas.

events.summary: In 2025 the commercial name became Racing Bulls, presented as Visa Cash App Racing Bulls. The constructor id used for the entry does not change.
events.preconditions: The owner was unchanged. A title sponsor and a commercial name could be added without a new Jolpica constructor.

events.summary: Renault stopped as an engine manufacturer at the end of 2025. Alpine then used Mercedes engines, as it had done under the Lotus name in 2015.
events.preconditions: The team already had a Mercedes supply in its past, so losing Renault engines did not require a new constructor entry.

events.summary: In February 2025 Williams announced a multi-year Atlassian title deal and raced 2025 as Atlassian Williams Racing. Near the end of that season it said the 2026 name would be Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
events.preconditions: Dorilton already owned the team. A software company could buy the title name without buying the entry.

events.summary: In December 2025 Toyota's partnership with Haas became a title deal and the team is presented as TGR Haas F1 Team.
events.preconditions: Haas already had a technical link with Toyota Gazoo Racing from October 2024. The title name did not change the constructor id or the Ferrari power unit.

events.summary: The Sauber Motorsport infobox gives 7 December 2025 as the end of the company. The entry continues as Audi in 2026.
events.preconditions: The sale to Audi was complete and the Sauber name was no longer the constructor. The date is the company record, not a race result.

events.summary: Audi has raced as a constructor and power-unit manufacturer from 2026, as Audi Revolut F1 Team, on the former Sauber entry.
events.preconditions: The purchase and the new power-unit rules were both in place. This is not the 1950-1951 or 1979-1985 Alfa Romeo works team.

events.summary: General Motors entered in 2026 as Cadillac Formula 1 Team, with TWG Motorsports, and the page calls it the first new independent constructor since Haas in 2016. A Cadillac power unit is expected in 2029, not in 2026.
events.preconditions: GM and an American motorsport group built a new entry across several US sites plus Silverstone. The 2026 engine is not described as a Cadillac works unit.

events.summary: The 2026 constructors table lists Ferrari as Cadillac's engine. Cadillac's own power unit is described as a later plan, from 2029.
events.preconditions: A new team needed an engine on day one. Ferrari could supply one before GM's own unit existed.

events.summary: Ford's engine table on its Formula One page has a new block from the 2026 Australian Grand Prix. Red Bull says it switched to Ford power in 2026 after signing the deal in 2023.
events.preconditions: Red Bull already had an entry and had been planning past the Honda supply. Ford's return is an engine partnership, not a new team.

events.preconditions: Aston Martin already had an entry and a Silverstone base. The change is a manufacturer supply, not a new team.
